q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Consolidated Fund of India from the Consolidated Fund of a State?

options.A: The Consolidated Fund of India receives all the revenues received and loans raised by the Government of India and moneys can be withdrawn from it only under appropriation made by law of Parliament, whereas the Consolidated Fund of a State receives the revenues and loans of that State and moneys can be withdrawn from it only under appropriation made by law of the Legislature of the State
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India is regulated by the Legislature of each State, whereas the Consolidated Fund of a State is regulated by Parliament
options.C: Both the Funds are placed at the disposal of the President for meeting urgent unforeseen expenditure
options.D: Moneys can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of a State without any appropriation, whereas withdrawals from the Consolidated Fund of India require appropriation by Parliament

q: The Department of Posts pays the Railways the charges for the carriage of postal mails in mail vans attached to passenger trains. In the railway accounts, these receipts are classified under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: Other Coaching Earnings

q: The gross earnings of a zonal railway for a year are Rs 5,000 crore and its total working expenses, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, are Rs 4,600 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway for the year is:

options.A: 108.7 per cent
options.B: 92 per cent
options.C: 8 per cent
options.D: 85 per cent

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Ways and Means Advances from Treasury Bills of the Government of India?

options.A: Ways and Means Advances are zero-coupon instruments issued in the market at a discount, whereas Treasury Bills are advances made by the Reserve Bank repayable within three months
options.B: Both Ways and Means Advances and Treasury Bills are advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government
options.C: Ways and Means Advances are advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to meet temporary mismatches in the cash flow of the Government, repayable not later than three months from the date of the advance, whereas Treasury Bills are zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at face value, in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days
options.D: Treasury Bills are repayable not later than three months from the date of issue, whereas Ways and Means Advances are issued in maturities of 91, 182 and 364 days

q: An officer of a zonal railway, expecting that a grant will be voted in due course, incurs expenditure on a service before the grant for it has been authorised, and no advance has been taken from the Contingency Fund of India. The correct position is that:

options.A: Expenditure in anticipation of a grant is not permissible — expenditure can be incurred only after the grant has been authorised, the advance from the Contingency Fund of India being the recognised exception
options.B: Expenditure in anticipation of a grant is permissible up to five per cent of the expected grant
options.C: Expenditure in anticipation of a grant is permissible in the month of March alone
options.D: Expenditure in anticipation of a grant is freely permissible at the discretion of the head of the office

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a refund of fares and freight from a recovery of an amount overpaid to a contractor?

options.A: Both a refund of fares and a recovery of an overpayment are treated as revenue receipts of the Railways
options.B: A refund of fares and freight granted to the public is treated as a deduction from the earnings of the Railways, whereas a recovery of an amount overpaid is treated as a reduction of expenditure, by way of a deduct entry under the head of account originally debited
options.C: A refund of fares is treated as a reduction of expenditure, whereas a recovery of an overpayment is treated as a deduction from earnings
options.D: A refund of fares is charged to the Contingency Fund of India, whereas a recovery of an overpayment is credited to the Public Account of India

q: The management of a zonal railway requires figures of the earnings of the railway at short intervals during the year, long before the station returns have been subjected to internal check and the earnings apportioned among the railways. The figures so compiled are the:

options.A: Accounted earnings, compiled after internal check and apportionment in the Traffic Book
options.B: Final earnings of the year as certified by Audit
options.C: Earnings as voted by Parliament in the Demands for Grants
options.D: Approximate earnings, compiled at intervals of ten days from the station returns, before internal check and apportionment

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the taxes referred to in Article 269 of the Constitution from the taxes referred to in Article 270?

options.A: The taxes under Article 269 are levied and collected by the Union but are assigned wholly to the States, their proceeds not forming part of the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas the taxes under Article 270 are levied and collected by the Union and are shared between the Union and the States in the manner prescribed
options.B: The taxes under Article 269 are shared between the Union and the States, whereas the taxes under Article 270 are assigned wholly to the States
options.C: Both the taxes under Article 269 and those under Article 270 are levied, collected and retained wholly by the Union
options.D: The taxes under Article 270 are levied by the States and collected by the Union, whereas the taxes under Article 269 are levied and collected by the States themselves

q: A Government officer receives, in his official capacity, court deposits and other moneys which are neither revenues nor public moneys of the Government. Under Article 284 of the Constitution, these moneys are required to be paid into the:

options.A: Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Public Account of India
options.D: Departmental account maintained with the accredited bank

q: A payment of Rs 8,400 is correctly recorded in the Cash Book of a railway, but in posting it to the Ledger the corresponding credit is entered as Rs 4,800 instead of Rs 8,400. The disagreement brought out in the Trial Balance on this account is:

options.D: Nil, an error in the amount posted being a compensating error

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Volume I of the Indian Railway Accounts Code from Volume II of the Code?

options.A: Volume I deals with Traffic Accounts and station accounts, whereas Volume II deals with the general accounts of a railway
options.B: Both the volumes deal only with the classification of accounts contained in the Finance Code
options.C: Volume I deals with the purchase and custody of stores, whereas Volume II deals with workshop accounts
options.D: Volume I contains the rules relating to the general accounts of the Railways, including the maintenance of books and the rendering of the Account Current, whereas Volume II deals with Traffic Accounts, including station accounts and the Traffic Book

q: During the course of a financial year, it is decided to change the allocation of a class of expenditure from one head of account to another. The change is given effect to in the accounts from:

options.A: The commencement of the next financial year
options.B: The date of the decision, with retrospective effect from the beginning of the current year
options.C: The March (Final) accounts of the current year itself
options.D: The month following the decision, within the same financial year

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'token grant' from a 'Vote of Credit'?

options.A: Both a token grant and a Vote of Credit are taken after the close of the year to regularise excess expenditure
options.B: A token grant is a grant for a service of an indefinite character, whereas a Vote of Credit is a nominal grant for a new service
options.C: A token grant is a nominal grant taken to obtain the approval of Parliament for a new service whose cost can be met by re-appropriation within the grant, whereas a Vote of Credit is granted where, on account of the magnitude or the indefinite character of the service, the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant
options.D: A token grant requires no approval of Parliament, whereas a Vote of Credit is authorised through the Contingency Fund of India

q: The receipts realised at a station from the sale of platform tickets to visitors are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Other Coaching Earnings
options.C: Goods earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

q: The Railway Board issues an amendment to the list of Major, Minor and other heads of account contained in the Indian Railway Finance Code, for adoption by all the zonal railways. The amendment is issued through:

options.A: A Transfer Certificate
options.B: An entry in the Pink Book
options.C: A Budget Circular of the Ministry of Finance
options.D: An Advance Correction Slip

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Ledger from the Trial Balance of a railway?

options.A: The Ledger is the principal book of account in which an account is maintained for every head of account, whereas the Trial Balance is the list of the balances extracted from the Ledger to test the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.B: The Trial Balance is the principal book of account, whereas the Ledger is extracted from it every month
options.C: Both the Ledger and the Trial Balance exhibit the assets and liabilities of the Railways
options.D: The Ledger is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Trial Balance is maintained by the Audit Department

q: The revenue receipts of the Government for a year are Rs 18,00,000 crore and its revenue expenditure for the year is Rs 21,50,000 crore. The revenue deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 39,50,000 crore
options.B: Rs 18,00,000 crore
options.C: Rs 3,50,000 crore
options.D: Nil, a revenue deficit arising only when there is also a fiscal deficit

q: An amount has stood debited to a suspense head for several years on account of services rendered to an outside party, and it is ultimately found that the party is untraceable and the amount is irrecoverable. The amount can be written off:

options.A: By the dealing assistant in the Accounts Office on his own authority
options.B: Only under the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Automatically at the close of the financial year in which it is found to be old
options.D: Only with the approval of Parliament through a Demand for Grant

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the compilation of the Finance Accounts of the Railways from the compilation of the Finance Accounts of the other Ministries of the Government of India?

options.A: Both the Railways and the other Ministries compile their Finance Accounts through the Pay and Accounts Offices of the Controller General of Accounts
options.B: The Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts, whereas those of the other Ministries are compiled by the Railway Board
options.C: The Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas those of the other Ministries are compiled by the Ministry of Finance
options.D: The consolidated Finance Accounts of the Railways are compiled by the Railway Board from the Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways and other accounting units, whereas the Finance Accounts of the Ministries whose accounts are compiled under the departmentalised system are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts

q: A member of the Rajya Sabha, during the discussion on the Budget, seeks to move a cut motion on the Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways. The correct position is that:

options.A: Cut motions on the Demands for Grants can be moved only in the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha being able to discuss the Budget but having no power to vote on the Demands or to move cut motions on them
options.B: A cut motion can be moved in the Rajya Sabha with the permission of its Chairman
options.C: A cut motion can be moved in the Rajya Sabha in respect of charged expenditure alone
options.D: A cut motion moved in the Rajya Sabha has the same effect as one moved in the Lok Sabha

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Financial Bill of the first category from a Financial Bill of the second category?

options.A: Both the categories of Financial Bills can be introduced in either House of Parliament without the recommendation of the President
options.B: A Financial Bill of the first category can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, whereas a Financial Bill of the second category can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha
options.C: A Financial Bill of the first category, which contains any of the matters specified in Article 110(1) together with other matters, shall not be introduced except on the recommendation of the President and shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, whereas a Financial Bill of the second category, which would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India but contains none of the matters specified in Article 110(1), can be introduced in either House, though it cannot be passed by either House unless the President has recommended its consideration
options.D: A Financial Bill of the second category is a Money Bill, whereas a Financial Bill of the first category is an ordinary Bill

q:
Consider the following statements about 'Cash-in-Transit' in the railway accounts:
1. Station earnings which have been remitted but have not yet been credited by the bank form a component of Cash-in-Transit.
2. Security deposits received from contractors, held under the 'Deposits' head, form a component of Cash-in-Transit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: An officer holds a sanctioned imprest of Rs 15,000. At a surprise check, the paid vouchers held by him in support of the expenditure incurred out of the imprest, and not yet recouped, amount to Rs 9,250. The cash in hand with the holder should be:
Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Miscellaneous Advances (Capital)' from 'Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue)' in railway accounts?

options.A: Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are operated as a revenue suspense head, whereas Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue) are carried in the capital classification
options.B: Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are carried in the capital (Plan Head) classification of railway expenditure, whereas Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue) are operated as a suspense head, pending recovery or adjustment
options.C: Both the heads represent deposits received from contractors, pending refund
options.D: Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are charged to the ordinary working expenses, whereas Miscellaneous Advances (Revenue) are charged to Capital

q: The separate Railway Budget, introduced following the Separation Convention of 1924, holds a special place in the Budget presented for the financial year 2016-17 because it was:

options.A: The first separate Railway Budget presented to Parliament
options.B: The first Railway Budget presented by the Finance Minister
options.C: The last occasion on which a separate Railway Budget was presented to Parliament, the Railway Budget being merged with the Union Budget from the following year
options.D: The only Railway Budget in which no Demands for Grants were voted

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Acworth Committee from the committee chaired by Bibek Debroy in relation to railway finances?

options.A: The Acworth Committee recommended the separation of railway finances from the general finances of the Government, leading to a separate Railway Budget, whereas the committee chaired by Bibek Debroy recommended the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget and the setting up of an independent regulator for the Railways
options.B: The Acworth Committee recommended the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, whereas the Debroy Committee recommended its separation
options.C: Both the committees recommended the continuance of a separate Railway Budget for the Railways
options.D: The Acworth Committee dealt only with the classification of accounts, whereas the Debroy Committee dealt only with the audit of railway accounts

q: A bill presented by an executive department is found, on internal check in the Accounts Office, to bear a wrong allocation. The primary responsibility for showing the correct allocation on the bill rests with:

options.A: The Accounts Officer who passes the bill for payment
options.B: The Cash & Pay Office which makes the payment
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The executive (departmental) officer who presents the bill

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the National Small Savings Fund from the National Investment Fund of the Government of India?

options.A: Both the funds are credited mainly with the proceeds of disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises
options.B: The National Small Savings Fund is maintained in the Public Account of India and holds the collections under the small savings schemes, its balances being invested in Central and State Government securities, whereas the National Investment Fund is credited mainly with the proceeds of disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises
options.C: The National Small Savings Fund is credited with disinvestment proceeds, whereas the National Investment Fund holds the small savings collections
options.D: The National Investment Fund is maintained in the Public Account of India for small savings, whereas the National Small Savings Fund forms part of the Consolidated Fund of India

q: Finding a large part of its grant still unspent in the closing months of the financial year, a division books a rush of expenditure in March mainly in order to avoid the lapse of the grant. Such a rush of expenditure is regarded in the financial rules as:

options.A: A breach of financial regularity and propriety, to be avoided
options.B: A sign of efficient utilisation of the grant
options.C: A desirable measure for preventing the lapse of grants
options.D: Permissible without any restriction in the closing month of the year

q: The total expenditure of the Government for a year is Rs 40,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 24,00,000 crore and its non-debt capital receipts are Rs 2,00,000 crore. The fiscal deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 16,00,000 crore
options.B: Rs 24,00,000 crore
options.C: Rs 26,00,000 crore
options.D: Rs 14,00,000 crore

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Capital Account from the Revenue Account in the annual commercial accounts of the Railways?

options.A: Both the Capital Account and the Revenue Account exhibit the earnings and working expenses of the year
options.B: The Capital Account exhibits the earnings of the year, whereas the Revenue Account exhibits the capital outlay of the Railways
options.C: The Capital Account exhibits the capital outlay of the Railways and the assets created out of it, as reflected in the Block Account, whereas the Revenue Account exhibits the earnings of the year against the working expenses of the year, so as to arrive at the net revenue or surplus of the year
options.D: The Revenue Account is a part of the Capital Account and shows the balances under the suspense heads alone

q: After the Demands for Grants have been voted, a member of the Lok Sabha proposes an amendment to the Appropriation Bill which would increase the amount provided for a service and divert it to another service. Under Article 114(2) of the Constitution, such an amendment:

options.A: Can be moved with the recommendation of the President
options.B: Is barred, no amendment being permissible which would have the effect of varying the amount, or altering the destination, of any grant already made by the House
options.C: Can be moved in the Rajya Sabha, though not in the Lok Sabha
options.D: Is permissible if the total amount of the Appropriation Bill remains unchanged

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Controller General of Accounts from the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

options.A: The Controller General of Accounts is the principal accounting adviser to the Government of India and compiles the accounts of the Ministries under the departmentalised system, whereas the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is the constitutional audit authority, the accounts of the Union and the States being kept in the form prescribed by the President on his advice
options.B: The Controller General of Accounts conducts the statutory audit of Government accounts, whereas the Comptroller and Auditor General of India compiles the accounts of the Ministries
options.C: Both the officers are appointed under Article 148 of the Constitution to conduct the audit of Government accounts
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is the accounting adviser of the Government, whereas the Controller General of Accounts heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department

q: A number of works in the Works Programme (Pink Book) of a railway are each of a value below the prescribed limit and are therefore not shown individually in the Programme. Such works are provided for in the Programme:

options.A: Only after a supplementary grant is obtained for each of them
options.B: In the Rolling Stock Programme, item by item
options.C: Under the head 'Other Specified Works' in every case
options.D: In bulk, as lump sum provisions

q: The Finance Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha and its declared provisions relating to customs and excise duties take provisional effect, but the Bill is not enacted within seventy-five days of its introduction. The position under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act is that:

options.A: The declared provisions continue to have the force of law indefinitely
options.B: The declared provisions are deemed to have been enacted from the date of the Budget
options.C: The declared provisions cease to have the force of law, and the excess collections made under them are refundable
options.D: The Finance Bill is taken up afresh as a Money Bill in the following session

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the borrowing power of the Union under Article 292 of the Constitution from the borrowing power of a State under Article 293?

options.A: Both the Union and a State may borrow without any limit fixed by law
options.B: The executive power of the Union extends to borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within such limits, if any, as may be fixed by Parliament by law, whereas a State may borrow upon the security of its Consolidated Fund within such limits, if any, as may be fixed by the Legislature of the State by law, and a State which has an outstanding loan from, or guaranteed by, the Government of India cannot raise a fresh loan without the consent of the Government of India
options.C: A State may borrow upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas the Union borrows upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of the State
options.D: The borrowing power of a State is fixed by Parliament by law, whereas the borrowing power of the Union is fixed by the Finance Commission

q: Over a period of years, the appropriations made from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of a railway remain inadequate in relation to the renewals and replacements falling due. The likely consequence is:

options.A: Accumulation of arrears of renewal and replacement of over-aged assets
options.B: An automatic transfer of funds from the Development Fund to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: A reduction in the Capital-at-charge of the Railways
options.D: An increase in the surplus of the Railways available for appropriation to the Capital Fund

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the General Financial Rules, 2017 from the Government Accounting Rules, 1990?

options.A: Both the Rules are issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India for the audit of Government accounts
options.B: The General Financial Rules are issued by the Controller General of Accounts, whereas the Government Accounting Rules are issued by the Department of Expenditure
options.C: The General Financial Rules lay down the forms of Government accounts, whereas the Government Accounting Rules lay down the financial principles for procurement
options.D: The General Financial Rules, issued by the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, lay down the general financial principles and procedures applicable to Government departments, whereas the Government Accounting Rules, issued by the Controller General of Accounts, lay down the rules relating to the forms and compilation of Government accounts

q: For the purchase of a costly item of equipment, budget provision exists in the sanctioned Budget of a railway, but the sanction of the authority competent to sanction the purchase has not been obtained. The executive proposes to go ahead with the purchase on the ground that budget provision itself authorises it. The correct position is that:

options.A: Budget provision in the sanctioned Budget by itself amounts to sanction for the expenditure
options.B: Budget provision dispenses with the need for a sanctioned estimate in every case
options.C: The mere existence of provision in the sanctioned Budget does not by itself amount to sanction — the sanction of the competent authority is separately necessary before the expenditure is incurred
options.D: Budget provision authorises the executive to invite tenders and place the order, sanction being obtained afterwards

q: In a year before the payment of dividend by the Railways to General Finances was discontinued, the net revenue of the Railways was insufficient to meet the full dividend liability computed on the Capital-at-charge. The unpaid portion of the dividend was carried to the:

options.A: Development Fund
options.B: Deferred Dividend Liability Account
options.C: Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Debt Service Fund

q: An item of expenditure is booked in the accounts of a railway under the head prescribed by the classification of accounts, although the budget provision for that class of expenditure happens to exist under a different head. This is because:

options.A: Correct classification is followed irrespective of the head under which budget provision exists
options.B: Budget provision automatically alters the classification of the item
options.C: The classification of an item is decided by the spending unit itself
options.D: The Accounts Office may ignore the classification wherever budget provision exists under any head

q: The Union Government proposes to make a grant to a State for a public purpose which falls outside the legislative competence of the Union. The grant is:

options.A: Barred, a Government being able to make grants only for purposes within its own legislative competence
options.B: Permissible only with the prior approval of the Finance Commission
options.C: Permissible only if the purpose is enumerated in the Union List
options.D: Permissible under Article 282 of the Constitution, the Union or a State being able to make grants for any public purpose, even if that purpose is not one with respect to which it may make laws

q: A zonal railway proposes that the appropriations to be made to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund for a year be fixed in the Budget Estimates themselves as a fixed percentage of the gross earnings of the year. The correct position is that such appropriations are determined:

options.A: Monthly, in equal instalments throughout the year
options.B: By the Railway Convention Committee, once in five years
options.C: At the close of the financial year, with reference to the actual surplus (net revenue) available for the year
options.D: In the Revised Estimates, with reference to the earnings of the first five months

q: During the voting on a Demand for Grant, a member of the Lok Sabha proposes that the amount of the Demand be increased so that a larger provision is made for a service. The Lok Sabha:

options.A: Can increase the Demand with the recommendation of the President
options.B: Cannot increase the amount of the Demand — it may assent to the Demand, refuse it or reduce the amount demanded, but it cannot increase it
options.C: Can increase the Demand if the Finance Minister concurs in the proposal
options.D: Can increase the Demand by passing a token cut motion

options.D: Nil, the Trial Balance still agrees

options.B: Rs 80,000 crore

options.A: Capital Fund
options.B: Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Debt Service Fund
options.D: Railway Safety Fund

q:
Consider the following statements:

options.A: 1 only

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

options.A: Revised Estimates of the year

options.C: Account Current of April of the next year
options.D: Supplementary Demands for Grants

q: A contractor whose bill was paid last month presents a copy of the same voucher again in support of a fresh claim, and the claim is rejected at once because the original voucher had been stamped 'Paid' and cancelled after the first payment. This stamping and cancellation of paid vouchers is done primarily in order to:

options.A: Enable the voucher to be destroyed immediately after payment
options.B: Indicate that the voucher has been checked by Audit
options.C: Help the Cash & Pay Office in preparing the Cash Book
options.D: Prevent the same voucher from being presented again in support of another claim for payment

q: The holder of a permanent imprest on a zonal railway is transferred from his post. Before handing over charge, he is required to:

options.A: Spend the unspent balance of the imprest before he leaves
options.B: Retain the imprest amount until his successor demands it
options.C: Account for the imprest in full and hand over the balance to his successor
options.D: Deposit the imprest balance in the Public Account in his own name

q: An advance is given to an officer for meeting the expenses of a specific occasion, and it is required to be accounted for as soon as that occasion is over. Such an advance is a:

options.A: Temporary imprest
options.B: Permanent (standing) imprest
options.C: Miscellaneous Advance (Capital)
options.D: Deposit work advance

q: At the close of a year, expenditure under one Sub-Major Head of a Demand exceeds the provision under that head, but savings are available under another Sub-Major Head of the same Demand and the total expenditure is within the total amount of the Grant. The position is correctly dealt with by:

options.A: Presenting a Demand for Excess Grant to Parliament
options.B: Regularising the excess under the Sub-Major Head by re-appropriation within the Grant
options.C: Writing off the excess with the sanction of the General Manager
options.D: Treating the whole Demand as having been exceeded

q: Anticipated savings under a grant are surrendered by a zonal railway during the course of the year. For the surrender to take effect:

options.A: The vote of the Lok Sabha on a Supplementary Demand is required
options.B: It is an executive act and does not require the approval of Parliament
options.C: A Supplementary Demand for Grants must first be presented
options.D: It can be made only after the Appropriation Accounts of the year are finalised

q: During a year, a zonal railway realises rent from a building let out to an outside party and charges for advertisements displayed on its station premises. These receipts are:

options.A: Apportioned among all the zonal railways in proportion to distance
options.B: Credited centrally to the Railway Board
options.C: Classified under Other Coaching Earnings and apportioned among the railways
options.D: Classified under Sundry Other Earnings and credited wholly to the railway on which they accrue, without apportionment

q: A passenger books a ticket and travels wholly within the limits of a single zonal railway, the traffic both originating and terminating on that railway. The earnings from this local traffic are:

options.A: Retained wholly by that railway, no apportionment being required
options.B: Apportioned among all the zonal railways
options.C: Credited to the Railway Board
options.D: Held under Traffic Suspense pending apportionment

q: The Government of India faces a temporary mismatch between its receipts and payments and obtains an advance from the Reserve Bank of India, repayable not later than three months from the date of the advance. The facility is:

options.A: Treasury Bills
options.B: Ways and Means Advances
options.C: Cash Management Bills
options.D: An advance from the Contingency Fund of India

q: The Government of India proposes to raise short-term funds for a period of about six months through Treasury Bills. The Treasury Bill maturity appropriate for the purpose is:

options.A: 91 days
options.B: 364 days
options.C: 182 days
options.D: 14 days

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India was enhanced in the year 2021 to Rs 30,000 crore.
2. The Contingency Fund of India is in the nature of an imprest placed at the disposal of the President, to enable advances to be made for meeting unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The separate Railway Budget was presented to Parliament for the last time for the financial year 2016-17.
2. The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget was recommended by the Acworth Committee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The market borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation form part of the internal debt of the Government of India.
2. The borrowings raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation are serviced by the Railways through lease charges.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ledger is the principal book of a railway, in which accounts are maintained for all the heads of account and from which the Trial Balance is extracted.
2. The Classified Abstract of a railway is prepared from its General Books.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' in the books of a zonal railway is invariably a debit balance.
2. Balances under 'Reserve Bank Suspense' are cleared on receipt of the advice or intimation from the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways, the actual expenditure of the year is compared with the Final Grant.
2. The Appropriation Accounts are laid before Parliament together with the Audit Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The separation of accounts from audit in the Union Government, that is, the departmentalisation of accounts, was introduced in the year 1976.
2. Under that arrangement, the accounts of the Railways were also taken over by the Controller General of Accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriations to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund are charged to the working expenses of the Railways, whether or not there is a surplus.
2. Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is made only out of the surplus available at the close of the financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'policy cut' motion from a 'token cut' motion moved on a Demand for Grant in the Lok Sabha?

options.A: A policy cut proposes a reduction of Rs 100 in order to ventilate a specific grievance, whereas a token cut reduces the Demand to Re 1
options.B: A policy cut reduces the Demand to Re 1 in order to express disapproval of the policy underlying the Demand, whereas a token cut proposes a reduction of Rs 100 in order to ventilate a specific grievance
options.C: Both a policy cut and a token cut propose a reduction of Rs 100 in the Demand
options.D: A policy cut can be moved only in the Rajya Sabha, whereas a token cut can be moved only in the Lok Sabha

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Capital Fund from the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Capital Fund is credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited with the proceeds of disinvestment
options.B: The Capital Fund is used for the renewal and replacement of existing assets, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund is used for the creation of new assets
options.C: Both the Capital Fund and the Depreciation Reserve Fund are credited with appropriations charged to the working expenses of the Railways
options.D: The Capital Fund is credited with appropriations made out of the surplus (net revenue) of the Railways and finances capital works out of internal resources, whereas the Depreciation Reserve Fund is charged to the working expenses and finances renewals and replacements of existing assets

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Cash-in-Transit' from 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' in railway accounts?

options.A: 'Cash-in-Transit' represents the station earnings which have been remitted but have not yet been credited by the bank, whereas 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' represents the balance of the Railways actually held with the Reserve Bank
options.B: 'Cash-in-Transit' represents the balance held with the Reserve Bank, whereas 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' represents the earnings still in transit from the stations
options.C: Both 'Cash-in-Transit' and 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' represent remittances which have not yet been credited by the bank
options.D: 'Cash-in-Transit' relates to the security deposits received from contractors, whereas 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' relates to the station earnings

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Transfer Certificate' from a 'Journal Voucher' in railway accounts?

options.A: A Transfer Certificate authorises a transfer entry within the books of a railway, whereas a Journal Voucher intimates a debit to another railway
options.B: Both a Transfer Certificate and a Journal Voucher intimate the debits raised against other railways
options.C: A Transfer Certificate is the advice through which a debit raised by one railway against another railway is intimated to the respondent railway, whereas a Journal Voucher is the document which authorises and records a transfer (journal) entry in the books of a railway
options.D: A Journal Voucher is issued by the Railway Board for inter-railway adjustments, whereas a Transfer Certificate is issued by the Cash & Pay Office for cash transactions

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh from the Special Railway Safety Fund?

options.A: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh was a one-time fund set up in 2001-02, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund is a continuing fund created from 2017-18
options.B: The Special Railway Safety Fund was a one-time fund set up in 2001-02 to wipe out the arrears of renewal and replacement of over-aged safety assets, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, created from 2017-18, provides an assured annual outlay for safety works financed through Gross Budgetary Support and the Railways' internal resources
options.C: Both the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh and the Special Railway Safety Fund were one-time funds set up in 2001-02
options.D: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is financed by the safety surcharge on passenger fares, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund is financed entirely by Gross Budgetary Support

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget Register from the Debt Head Report of a railway?

options.A: The Budget Register shows the balances outstanding under the debt heads, whereas the Debt Head Report is maintained to watch the expenditure against the budget allotments
options.B: Both the Budget Register and the Debt Head Report show the balances under the suspense heads of account
options.C: The Budget Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Debt Head Report is prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Budget Register is maintained in the Accounts Office to watch the expenditure against the budget allotment under each head of account, whereas the Debt Head Report shows the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the life of a cheque issued by the Railways which is not encashed by the payee?

options.A: Cheque issued — the period of validity of three months expires and the cheque becomes time-barred — the amount is written back in the books through a transfer entry — the payee surrenders the time-barred cheque and a fresh payment is made
options.B: Cheque issued — the amount is written back in the books through a transfer entry — the period of validity of three months expires — the payee surrenders the time-barred cheque and a fresh payment is made
options.C: The period of validity of three months expires — cheque issued — the amount is written back in the books through a transfer entry — a fresh payment is made
options.D: Cheque issued — the period of validity of three months expires and the cheque becomes time-barred — a fresh payment is made — the amount is written back in the books through a transfer entry

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in obtaining the approval of Parliament for expenditure on a 'New Service' not contemplated in the approved Budget, where the funds for the service can be found by re-appropriation within the grant?

options.A: Token grant voted by the Lok Sabha — the proposal is examined with reference to para 370 of the Finance Code — the amount is authorised through the Appropriation Act — a token grant is sought through the Supplementary Demands for Grants
options.B: The amount is authorised through the Appropriation Act — a token grant is sought through the Supplementary Demands for Grants — the proposal is examined with reference to para 370 of the Finance Code — token grant voted by the Lok Sabha
options.C: The proposal is examined with reference to para 370 of the Finance Code — a token grant is sought through the Supplementary Demands for Grants — the token grant is voted by the Lok Sabha — the amount is authorised through the Appropriation Act
options.D: A token grant is sought through the Supplementary Demands for Grants — the amount is authorised through the Appropriation Act — the proposal is examined with reference to para 370 of the Finance Code — the token grant is voted by the Lok Sabha

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Main Cash Book from the Ledger of a railway?

options.A: The Main Cash Book records, in chronological order, all the cash receipts and payments effected through the Cash and Pay Office, whereas the Ledger is a General Book in which the transactions are posted in classified form under the heads of account
options.B: The Main Cash Book is a General Book containing the classified postings, whereas the Ledger records the cash transactions of the Cash and Pay Office in chronological order

options.D: The Main Cash Book is maintained in the Traffic Accounts Office, whereas the Ledger is maintained at the stations
